(Half of −4 with its sign kept, −2, gives the bracket, not the coordinate.) So (2, −3).

problems.explain: ∠ACB and ∠ADB both stand on arc AB from the same side, and each is half of it. So ∠ADB = 90 ÷ 2 = 45°, and so is the other angle on that arc. (Not 90°: that would be the central angle.) So ∠ADB = 45°.

problems.explain: Each tangent meets its radius at 90°, so in quadrilateral OAPB two angles are 90° and the four add to 360°: ∠AOB + ∠APB = 180°. So it is 180 − 96 = 84°. (The two are supplementary, not equal.) So 84°.
